answer: Grow trust like a vine on karst: slowly, rooted in cracks that took time to form. An identity's reward cap rises only with each epoch it answers and passes grading, so a farm must pay to run every fake, every epoch, for weeks (length is an assumption) before any of them earns much; cheap mass signups buy nothing. Evasion: a patient farmer who funds the whole ramp, so this raises cost, it doesn't block. Wrongly hit: honest newcomers and agents knocked out by outages, so a missed epoch pauses growth instead of cutting the thread, and new caps still pay something.
